current_inference.orientation: Direct manipulation evidence outside Asteraceae supports multiple mechanisms (effective pollination plus abiotic protection) reaching seed/fruit fitness; effect transport to Cirsium remains a hypothesis.
current_inference.stickiness: A universal sticky-is-defence rule is not retained. Direct floral evidence includes strong benefit in Bejaria and a Cirsium null elsewhere in the repository, while whole-plant Datura shows substantial costs; context-dependent defence is the working hypothesis.
current_inference.display: Direct manipulation supports simultaneous pollinator-attraction benefit and seed-predator cost, but numerical common-effect extraction is not yet complete for the broad-angiosperm lane.
current_inference.bract_defence: Pedicularis rex directly separates functions: draining water-holding bracts left pollinator visitation unchanged but increased seed predation and reduced final seed set. This supports a defence/protection pathway rather than a generic pollinator-attraction function.
current_inference.colour_pigmentation: Silene UV exclusion shows that UV exposure induces anthocyanin while simultaneously depressing pollen and whole-plant seed production. This supports UV as a plausible selection pressure and pigment-induction context, but does not demonstrate that darker pigmentation itself raises fitness.

claim_boundary: Candidate calibration/effect-extraction registry only. It does not estimate a pooled across-angiosperm effect or prove adaptation in Cirsium.
